[EFFECT]
The model treats `weekday` as a categorical feature (0 = Sunday through 6 = Saturday), and its effect is non-monotonic. Sunday stands out with the largest negative contribution (≈ −0.065 in log space), meaning demand is modestly suppressed relative to the average. Monday and Tuesday are roughly neutral, Wednesday through Saturday all have positive contributions, and Friday (weekday = 5) is the clear peak at ≈ +0.041 — the day on which the model predicts the highest boost to hourly rentals. Saturday's contribution is also positive but noticeably lower than Friday's.

[IMPORTANCE]
`Weekday` ranks **7th out of 9 features** with an importance score of 0.024 — making it one of the weaker drivers of demand in this model. It is dwarfed by the top three features (hour of day, temperature, and year), and also sits below humidity, weather situation, and month; only wind speed and holiday have less influence.

[RECOMMENDATION]
Since Fridays consistently show the highest predicted demand boost and Sundays the lowest, it is worth ensuring slightly higher bike availability and staffing on Fridays while treating Sundays as lower-priority days — but keep in mind this is a secondary lever; optimising for busy commuter hours and warm-weather days will have a far greater operational impact.
